title: Text of PM’s interaction with India's CWG champions
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Prime Minister's Office Text of PM’s interaction with India's CWG champions प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                10 AUG 2026 1:11PM by PIB Delhi प्रधानमंत्री – मेरे यहां, मुझे यहां लगभग 12-13 साल हो गए इसी मकान में, अगर मैंने regularly और हर बार किसी को रिसिव किया है, किसी को मैं मिला हूं, तो खिलाड़ी हैं। पिछले 10-12 साल हो गए, आप लोगों के पुरुषार्थ के कारण, भारत को लगातार विजय दिलाने के आपके प्रयासों के कारण और उत्तरोत्तर सफलता में नई ऊंचाईयां पार करने की परंपरा के कारण, जो काम शायद हम स्कूलों में जाकर कहें कि नहीं नहीं भई खेलना चाहिए, ये करना चाहिए, वो काम स्कूलों में जाकर के हम कर सकते थे, उससे ज्यादा आपका मेडल उनको inspire करता है। प्रधानमंत्री – तुमने मुझे वादा किया था पिछली बार कि तुम्हारी दोनों बेटियां खिलाड़ी बन जाएंगी? खिलाड़ी - हाँ जी अभी वे उमर की छोटी हैं, अगले कॉमनवेल्थ में एक घर में तीन मेडल लाकर दिखाएंगी। प्रधानमंत्री – पक्का। खिलाड़ी – हाँ जी। खिलाड़ी – जब मैं दौड़ रहा था, जब मेरा इवेंट था 29 को, तो उस दिन गुरुपूर्णिमा थी, तो उस दिन मेरे गुरू को मैंने एक गिफ्ट दे दिया। प्रधानमंत्री – बड़ी शान बढ़ाई आपने। इतनी आंसू टपक रहे थे, मुझे लगता है कि आंसू के हर बूंद से जैसे गोल्ड मेडल टपक रहा है। खिलाड़ी – मैं बहुत ज्यादा खुशी थी, इमोशनल भी थे उसी दिन, खुशी ज्यादा था और मैं इसलिए रोई थी कि मेरा पेरिस आलंपिक में मेरा 1 Kg में मेडल रह गई थी और एक प्लेयर्स की लाइफ में क्या क्या हमको फेस करना पड़ता है। तो ये 4 साल के अंदर में कितना क्या क्या कुछ मैंने फेस किया था, हर टाइम injury ही चल रहे थे और family problem, वो सब हो रहा था। तो बहुत मुश्किल से मैं ये 4 साल फेस किया था। तो वो सब जब पोडियम में जब मैं खड़ी थी सर और हमारी जो फ्लैग ऊपर जाते हैं और हमारे नेशनल एंथम जब बजते हैं तो सर हम रुक नहीं सकते सर, अपना आप आंसू निकलते हैं। प्रधानमंत्री – बहुत बहुत बढ़िया प्रधानमंत्री – आपके इस अचीवमेंट को सिर्फ आपका अचीवमेंट मानता हूं, ऐसा नहीं है, ये आपका विजय आने वाली पीढ़ियों के लिए बहुत बड़ी प्रेरणा बन जाता है। खिलाड़ी – सब डर रहे थे हमसे कि इंडिया के साथ फाइट आ गई, अब तो हम पहली फाइट ही हार जायेंगे, हमारा मेडल भी नहीं आयेगा। प्रधानमंत्री – यानी मान के चलते हैं। खिलाड़ी – हाँ सर। प्रधानमंत्री – क्या हुआ, वो restaurant वालों से झगड़ा कर रही थी? खिलाड़ी – हम लोगों का जो इतना अच्छा परफॉर्मेंस था, लास्ट डे था और सब जीत के गए थे और पूरा इंडिया के लोग थे। तो थोड़ा सा मुझे बुरा लग रहा। तो मैंने उनको अच्छे से बोला रिक्वेस्ट किया था सर, फिर उन्होंने मान भी लिया, अभी चेंज भी हो गया सर। प्रधानमंत्री – इस विजय की परिस्थिति खुशी, आनंद, अपने साथियों के साथ और गेम पूरे हो चुके हैं। तो हसी मजाक मस्ती का मूड ऐसे समय उस मैप पर नजर जाना और उसको रजिस्टर करना और तुरंत सिर्फ मेडल लेते समय देश खड़ा हो जाता है ऐसा नहीं, भीतर से देश का भाव मैं सच बताता हूँ ये वीडियो सामान्य नहीं है आपका, लंबे समय तक लोगों को याद रहेगा। ये बॉक्सिंग वालों से भी दुनिया के खिलाड़ी अब डरने लगे हैं। खिलाड़ी – जरूर सर, पुरे सभी डरे हुए थे। एक के बाद एक गोल्ड मेडल गोल्ड मेडल आ रहे थे और मतलब पूरा लास्ट में ऐसे धमाका जैसा हो गया बिल्कुल। जिस तरीके से हम लोगों को सपोर्ट मिल रहा है, हमें बैक टू बैक कंपटीशन मिल रहा है वो एक बहुत बड़ी बात है और हमारे जितने भी यंग एथलीट है वो लोग सभी जैसे खेलो इंडिया स्कीम से आए हुए हैं और ये एक बहुत बड़ा changes ला रहा है पूरे स्पोर्ट्स में ही। प्रधानमंत्री – अगर आप लोग खेलो इंडिया की प्रतिष्ठा बढ़ाते हैं और प्रतिष्ठा सिर्फ वहां जाकर के रिबिन काटने से नहीं होगी। आप वैसे ही खेलेंगे जैसे एक छोटा विद्यार्थी, एक छोटा नौजवान, छोटा खिलाड़ी खेलता है। यह बहुत बड़ा कंट्रीब्यूशन करेगा। क्योंकि अभी तो हमें बहुत आगे जाना है, बहुत मेडल लाना है। कारगिल विजय दिवस पर किसकी विजय हुई थी? खिलाड़ी – उस दिन कारगिल डे था वैसे और जिस दिन मैंने पाकिस्तान के साथ फाइट किया था सर, वो उसी दिन का था। तो मैं एक इंडियन आर्मी से हूं, तो मैंने उस दिन मैं पहले से बहुत वो था कि सर पाकिस्तान को हराना है। तो मैंने वो पाकिस्तान एक तरफ मैंने 5-0 से हराया, तो मैंने हमारा इंडियन आर्मी का कारगिल हीरोज़ को मैंने डेडिकेट किया किया था सर। प्रधानमंत्री – आपको यह याद रहना और आप स्वयं फौज से हैं तो, मैं जरूर मानता हूं कि देश के वीर जवानों को आपने जो भाव प्रकट किया ना कि, मैं कारगिल के विजेताओं को मेरा मेडल समर्पित करता हूं। उसने उस विजय पर चार चांद लगा दिए और जिसको पराजित करना था उसी को किया आपने। खिलाड़ी – वो पाकिस्तान की बात चल रही है, मुझे किस्सा याद आ गया सर। 2015 वर्ल्ड मिलिट्री गेम थे और मेरी पाकिस्तान के साथ पहली फाइट आ गई थी और वर्ल्ड मिलिट्री गेम थे तो मिलिट्री वाले के फोन आए कि भई पाकिस्तान से नहीं हारना है। तो फिर मैं फर्स्ट राउंड 4-1 से जीत गया। सेकंड राउंड 3-2 से जीत गया, पर दोनों के सर लग गए आपस में, तो दोनों के लग गए कट और फाइट तो मैं जीत गया। प्रधानमंत्री – हाँ खिलाड़ी – उसके बाद फिर दोनों चले गए हॉस्पिटल में टांके लगवाने के लिए। फिर 2014 में आप फर्स्ट टाइम प्रधानमंत्री जी बने थे और जो हमारे साथ आर्मी का कोच गया हुआ था उसका नाम नरेंद्र राणा था और फिर वो कई देर तक सोच के मेरे को बोला कि भाईजान एक बात बोलूं, मैं हां बोलो, बोला भाईजान आपका नाम नरेंद्र है। आपके कोच का नाम नरेंद्र है, आपके प्रधानमंत्री का नाम नरेंद्र है, तो मुझे नरेंद्र नाम से नफरत हो गई है। प्रधानमंत्री – सिर्फ आपने मेडल की संख्या बढ़ाई ऐसा नहीं है। आपने एक पीढ़ी को तैयार किया। खिलाड़ी – मेरे मन में भी धक-धक धक-धक हो रहा है सर। प्रधानमंत्री – आप चिंता मत कीजिए। खिलाड़ी – पर.. प्रधानमंत्री – आप चाहें तो आपको बोलने में भी मेडल मिलने वाला है। खिलाड़ी – मेरे फ्रेंड सर्कल में किसी ने बोला था कि मैं उनको कुछ बोलती थी भई तुम्हारे अच्छे के लिए तुम करो। तो अक्सर मुझे वो बोलते थे कि तू के मोदी ते मिल रही है? प्रधानमंत्री – हाँ खिलाड़ी – हरियाणवी में बोल देते हैं सर कि क्या तू मोदी से मिली हुई है, कि तेरी बात माने। तो आज मैं आपसे मिली हूं सर। मैं उनको बोल पाऊंगी कि हां मैं मोदी जी से मिली हूं। खिलाड़ी – कॉमनवेंल्थ गेम्स में मैंने सिल्वर मेडल जीता, फिर मैंने क्रेडिट साहब को दिया, सपना तो था एक बार मेडल जीत के लेके आने के लिए, बट ट्रेनिंग का सेंटर नहीं था, मैंने SAI आने के बाद मैं बहुत ट्रेनिंग करके मेडल जीत पा रहा, इसलिए बहुत खुशी से मैंने सर को क्रेडिट दिया था क्योंकि बहुत इंप्रूव हुआ। प्रधानमंत्री – मेरे लिए बहुत बड़ा सम्मान का विषय है, मेहनत आपने की और मुझे याद किया, मैं आपका बहुत आभारी हूं दोस्त। प्रधानमंत्री – वाराणसी में खेल तुम प्रैक्टिस कर रही थी ना? खिलाड़ी – जी सर। प्रधानमंत्री – कैसा बना है स्टेडियम? खिलाड़ी – सर अच्छा बना है, वहां पर मैं 10-12 दिन के लिए ट्रेनिंग करने गई थी, क्योंकि मैं मंदिर गई थी तो वहां पर ही ट्रेनिंग करके आई थी। और मैं वहां पे मतलब सेटल भी होना चाहती हूं क्योंकि मुझे काशी विश्वनाथ बहुत अच्छा लगता है सर। प्रधानमंत्री – भोपाल में ट्रेनिंग कर रही थी ना? खिलाड़ी – जी सर। प्रधानमंत्री – कैसा बना है स्टेडियम? खिलाड़ी – सर अच्छा बना है, वहां पर मैं 10-12 दिन के लिए ट्रेनिंग करने गई थी, क्योंकि मैं मंदिर गई थी तो वहां पर ही ट्रेनिंग करके आई थी। और मैं वहां पे मतलब सेटल भी होना चाहती हूं क्योंकि मुझे काशी विश्वनाथ बहुत अच्छा लगता है सर। प्रधानमंत्री – भोपाल में ट्रेनिंग कर रही थी ना? खिलाड़ी – जी सर। प्रधानमंत्री – तो उज्जैन जाते थे कि नहीं? खिलाड़ी – जी सर उज्जैन भी गई थी सर। प्रधानमंत्री – अच्छा महाकाल के पास भी गई। खिलाड़ी – जी सर। प्रधानमंत्री – काशी विश्वनाथ के पास हो आई एक बार। खिलाड़ी – जी सर। प्रधानमंत्री – सावन महीना तो अभी है। खिलाड़ी – वहां घर जाके फिर उसके बाद जाऊंगी सर। प्रधानमंत्री – ठीक है। खिलाड़ी – साई ने भी सर बहुत सपोर्ट किया है मुझे। इसके कारण ही मैं यहां तक पहुंची हूं सर। और मैं खेलो इंडिया स्कीम में भी थी 2018 में जो फर्स्ट खेलो इंडिया हुआ था, उसमें मेरा सिल्वर मेडल था, वहां पे भी मैंने आपको देखा था ओपनिंग सेरेमनी में, तो उसमें मेरा मेडल था, तो मेरे को स्कीम भी मिल गया और मैं यहां तक पहुंची हूं सर। प्रधानमंत्री – स्पोर्ट्स व्यवस्था एक बात है, लेकिन देश मेडल तब प्राप्त करता है जब देश में स्पोर्ट्स कल्चर बनता है। दोस्तों आपने बहुत बड़ा काम किया है। देश का नाम रोशन किया है। आपको मैं बहुत बधाई देता हूं और आप विश्वास कीजिए आगे भी आप विजयी होंगे और फिर से एक बार यहीं पर हम मिलेंगे। बहुत-बहुत धन्यवाद। बहुत-बहुत शुभकामनाएं। प्रधानमंत्री – ये लगातार तीसरी बार देश को मेडल दिलवाया है। खिलाड़ी – थैंक यू सर। प्रधानमंत्री – बहुत आशीर्वाद बेटा। खिलाड़ी – और थैंक यू सो मच मैं सर के हाथ से लड्डू खा रही मेरा कल बर्थडे था तो आज सर के हाथ से… प्रधानमंत्री – बहुत बधाई वाह। प्रधानमंत्री – मुस्कुराओ यार । प्रधानमंत्री – जो खेलेगा वो खिलेगा। **** MJPS/SS/ST/SS/DK/RK (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2297002)

title: DGFT Removes Physical Duty Payment Challans for Export Obligation Discharge Certificate Applications under Advance Authorisation and Export Promotion Capital Goods Schemes
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Commerce & Industry DGFT Removes Physical Duty Payment Challans for Export Obligation Discharge Certificate Applications under Advance Authorisation and Export Promotion Capital Goods Schemes Physical Challans Dispensed with for Voluntary Duty Payments from 1 August 2026 DGFT–ICEGATE API Integration Enables Direct Access to Authenticated Customs Duty Payment Records प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                10 AUG 2026 1:29PM by PIB Delhi In a significant Ease of Doing Business measure for exporters, the Directorate General of Foreign Trade (DGFT) has removed the requirement of submitting physical duty payment challans while applying for Export Obligation Discharge Certificates (EODC) under the Advance Authorisation (AA) and Export Promotion Capital Goods (EPCG) Schemes. Licence-wise voluntary duty payment data received from Customs/ICEGATE has been integrated with DGFT’s online systems, enabling authenticated verification of such payments directly against the concerned authorisation. For voluntary duty payments made on or after 1 August 2026, exporters will no longer be required to submit physical challans along with their applications for closure of authorisations. Authenticated payment details will be made available to exporters on the DGFT Customer Portal, enabling them to verify that the payment has been correctly mapped to the concerned authorisation before filing the application. The same authenticated payment record will be available to the Regional Authorities on the DGFT Back Office, eliminating the need for manual verification of payment particulars. This is expected to facilitate faster processing, reduce avoidable correspondence and bring greater consistency in decision-making across DGFT Regional Authorities. The digital facility has been implemented through an API-based data exchange between DGFT and ICEGATE, under which duty payment particulars are transmitted electronically from Customs systems to DGFT’s EODC processing workflow. The replacement of manual submission and verification with authenticated digital records is expected to shorten processing timelines, improve data accuracy, minimise human intervention and enhance transparency in the closure process. The measure is also expected to reduce transaction costs and compliance burden for exporters by reducing documentation, follow-up and physical interface, particularly benefiting MSME exporters handling closure formalities in-house. Trade Notice No. 15/2026-27 dated 5 August 2026 has been issued by DGFT for information of exporters and other stakeholders. The initiative is part of the Government’s broader digital transformation agenda for trade facilitation, aimed at creating a more efficient, predictable and trust-based regulatory environment. By strengthening integration between trade-related digital systems and reducing reliance on physical documentation, the measure reinforces the vision of “Minimum Government, Maximum Governance” and enables exporters to focus on trade and growth. The Advance Authorisation Scheme permits duty-free import of inputs that are physically incorporated in the export product, while the EPCG Scheme permits import of capital goods at concessional or zero customs duty, in both cases against an export obligation. Where the export obligation is not fulfilled in full, the authorisation holder regularises the case by voluntarily paying the proportionate customs duty saved along with applicable interest and thereafter applies for an EODC to close the authorisation. Earlier, proof of such payment was required to be submitted in physical form and verified manually by the Regional Authority. title: Asiatic Lion population rises from 523 in 2015 to 891 in 2025; Reflects dedication of Forest Officials, Conservationists and Local Communities: Shri Bhupender Yadav
content:

                10 AUG 2026 12:02PM by PIB Delhi On World Lion Day 2026, Union Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change, Shri Bhupender Yadav, celebrated India’s remarkable journey in lion conservation and reaffirmed the country’s unwavering commitment to protecting wildlife and biodiversity. In a post on social media, the Minister noted that the Asiatic Lion population has steadily increased from 523 in 2015 to 891 in 2025. He attributed this achievement to the dedication of forest officials, conservationists, local communities and all those working tirelessly to protect the magnificent species. 🦁 On World Lion Day, we celebrate India’s remarkable journey in lion conservation. India’s success in conserving the Asiatic Lion is a proud testament to our unwavering commitment to wildlife and biodiversity. He reaffirmed the resolve to safeguard India’s natural heritage and ensure that the roar of the Asiatic Lion continues to resonate for generations to come. On the occasion, in a social media post, Union MoS (EFCC), Shri Kirti Vardhan Singh, stated that by protecting critical habitats, strengthening conservation programmes and fostering coexistence, India has shown the world that development and nature can thrive together. content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Minority Affairs Welfare Schemes for Hill-Based Minority Communities implemented by  Ministry of Minority Affairs प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                10 AUG 2026 2:07PM by PIB Delhi Ministry of Minority Affairs implements the following schemes/programmes for socio-economic empowerment of the six (6) centrally notified minority communities namely Buddhists, Christians, Jains, Muslims, Parsis and Sikhs across the country including the state of West Bengal irrespective of any topographic conditions: 1. PRADHAN MANTRI VIRASAT KA SAMVARDHAN (PM VIKAS) The Ministry of Minority Affairs is implementing Pradhan Mantri Virasat Ka Samvardhan (PM VIKAS), an integrated Central Sector Scheme by combining the five erstwhile livelihood schemes, namely Seekho Aur Kamao, USTTAD, Hamari Dharohar, Nai Roshni and Nai Manzil, to facilitate opportunities for minority communities in education, skilling and employment. The Scheme comprises four components, namely (i) Skilling and Training, (ii) Women Leadership and Entrepreneurship, (iii) Education, and (iv) Infrastructure Development through convergence with Pradhan Mantri Jan Vikas Karyakram (PMJVK), wherever required. 2. PRADHAN MANTRI JAN VIKAS KARYAKRAM (PMJVK) PMJVK, a Centrally Sponsored Scheme aims to create community infrastructure in Minority Concentration Areas across the country in sectors such as Health, Education, Skill Development, Women-centric Projects, Drinking Water and Sanitation, Sports, Renewable Energy and other community infrastructure. 3. CONCESSIONAL CREDIT SCHEMES OF NATIONAL MINORITIES DEVELOPMENT & FINANCE CORPORATION (NMDFC) So far as NMDFC is concerned, it is functioning to promote the socio-economic development of the notified minority communities, namely Muslims, Christians, Sikhs, Buddhists, Parsis and Jains, across the country, including hill-based minority communities. Under Credit Line-1 (CL-1) , persons having an annual family income of up to ₹3.00 lakh are eligible for financial assistance under NMDFC schemes. Under Credit Line-2 (CL-2) , persons having an annual family income of up to ₹8.00 lakh are eligible for financial assistance. NMDFC implements its concessional credit schemes through State Channelising Agencies (SCAs) nominated by the respective State Governments/UT Administrations. In the State of West Bengal, the West Bengal Minorities Development & Finance Corporation (WBMDFC) is the designated State Channelising Agency and implements NMDFC schemes for eligible minority beneficiaries, including those belonging to hill-based minority communities, in accordance with the prescribed guidelines. title: DEVELOPMENT OF TOURISM IN THE NORTH-EASTERN REGION
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Tourism DEVELOPMENT OF TOURISM IN THE NORTH-EASTERN REGION प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                10 AUG 2026 3:01PM by PIB Delhi Ministry of Tourism as part of its ongoing endeavour, promotes various tourism destinations and products of India including the states of North Eastern region in a holistic manner, through various initiatives including promotional events, assistance to State Governments/UT Administrations for organising fairs and festivals, participation in exhibitions, websites, social media etc. The Ministry of Tourism has been organizing International Tourism Mart (ITM) in the North Eastern Region since 2013. The ITM is an annual event designed to highlight the tourism potential of the North Eastern region for both domestic and international audiences. This event serves as a vital platform, bringing together tourism businesses and entrepreneurs from the eight North Eastern States—Assam, Arunachal Pradesh, Manipur, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland, Tripura, and Sikkim—to foster collaboration and interactions among buyers, sellers, media, government agencies, and other stakeholders. The latest   ITM was held at Gangtok, Sikkim, from 13-16 November 2025. In addition to this the followings steps including the initiatives under various central schemes as under: (i) Incredible India Digital Platform-The Ministry of Tourism revamped the Incredible India website as IIDP in September 2024 to engage the visitors across web and social media platforms. The content on the Incredible India Website is available in Hindi, English and UN languages. The website features tourism destination in the North East States to promote tourism in NER. (ii)The Ministry of Tourism promotes various tourism sites and products in North East Region in the domestic and international markets. Creative posts, Live sessions, Tweets etc., on North East destinations are posted on regular basis on the social media handles of the Ministry of Tourism. In addition, the Ministry of Tourism also produces promotional material showcasing the tourist destinations and products in North Eastern States. (iii)Central Financial Assistance (CFA) support for organizing fairs & festivals- Ministry of Tourism provides financial assistance to State Governments/UT Administrations for organising fairs / festivals and Tourism related events under the DPPH scheme. The list of North East States to which the financial support for organizing fairs and festivals has been extended is at Annexure-II. (iv) Ministry of Tourism under the schemes of ‘Swadesh Darshan’, ‘National Mission on Pilgrimage Rejuvenation and Spiritual Heritage Augmentation Drive (PRASHAD)’, ‘Assistance to Central Agencies for Tourism Infrastructure Development’ provides financial assistance to State Governments/Union Territory Administrations/Central Agencies, Special Assistance to States for Capital Investment (SASCI Scheme), Challenge Based Destination Development (CBDD) for the development of tourism related infrastructure and facilities at various tourism destinations in the country including North Eastern Region. The Ministry of Tourism has now revamped the Swadesh Darshan Scheme as Swadesh Darshan 2.0 (SD 2.0) with the objective to develop sustainable and responsible tourism destinations, following a destination & tourism centric approach. The details of projects sanctioned under the above-mentioned schemes in North Eastern region are given at Annexure-III. Ministry of Tourism implements the Swachhta Action Plan (SAP) in coordination with the Department of Drinking Water & Sanitation, Ministry of Jal Shakti. Under SAP, the Ministry conducts cleanliness-awareness programmes, including in the North Eastern States. During 2025–26, 200 SAP activities were organized through IITTM, Central IHMs, State IHMs and FCIs under the following categories of (i) Tourist Awareness (ii) Students Awareness (iii) Stakeholders Awareness. Additionally, as directed by the Ministry of Jal Shakti, the Ministry of Tourism observes Swachhta Pakhwada and Swachhta Hi Sewa (SHS) every year in September and October. In 2025, 277 activities under Swachhta Pakhwada and 244 activities under SHS were carried out across India, including the North Eastern Region. For effective air connectivity at PAN Indian basis including the States of NER, the Ministry of Civil Aviation launched the RCS-UDAN scheme to make regional air travel affordable, and the Ministry of Tourism has collaborated with it by extending Viability Gap Funding under the Champion Service Sector Scheme to improve air links to key tourist locations, including in the North Eastern Region. Under this initiative, the following NER routes have been included as Tourism RCS routes: Dibrugarh–Dimapur, Dimapur–Dibrugarh, Dimapur–Imphal, Imphal–Dimapur, Agartala–Aizawl, Aizawl–Agartala, Dibrugarh–Imphal, Imphal–Dibrugarh, Hollongi–Guwahati and Guwahati–Hollongi. title: PAIMANA: Strengthening Data-Driven Infrastructure Governance
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau PIB Backgrounder PAIMANA: Strengthening Data-Driven Infrastructure Governance प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                10 AUG 2026 11:47AM by PIB Delhi PAIMANA – An Overview Efficient monitoring of infrastructure projects is essential for timely implementation, transparency and governance. To support this, PAIMANA (Project Assessment, Infrastructure Monitoring and Analytics for Nation-Building) was launched on 25 September 2025 as a web-based platform for monitoring Central Sector infrastructure projects in India. The platform replaces the earlier OCMS-2006 (Online Computerized Monitoring System). Developed by the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI), PAIMANA is used for monitoring ongoing Central Sector infrastructure projects costing ₹150 crore or more. MoSPI has launched a module called PAIMANA-CRIP on 08 th July 2026, replacing DPIIT’s Integrated Project Monitoring Portal (IPMP), envisioned to evolve as Central Repository of Infrastructure Projects. The project-related data for PRAGATI (Pro-Active Governance and Timely Implementation), PMG and other review mechanisms would subsequently be sourced and updated through the same. Over 20+ Ministries/Departments/ Implementing Agencies regularly update the information of projects on PAIMANA-CRIP through data entry or via API (Application Programming Interfaces) modes. Currently, the Project Monitoring vertical of the PAIMANA portal is integrated with DPIIT’s IPMP/ IIG through API-based data exchange. Over 60 per cent of projects on PAIMANA are being updated automatically through APIs from the MIS or web platforms of respective Ministries/ Departments. In addition to strengthening project monitoring, PAIMANA has expanded its role to support infrastructure performance monitoring through a dedicated Performance Monitoring Dashboard. Launched on 16 th April, 2026, the dashboard tracks infrastructure performance across major sub-sectors through a comprehensive set of indicators. It marks a significant advancement towards data-driven governance and evidence-based policymaking. Performance Monitoring Dashboard at a Glance The Performance Monitoring Dashboard brings together performance indicators across key infrastructure sectors in a unified digital platform. The indicators are compiled from official data provided/published by the concerned Ministries and Departments and are updated periodically based on the latest available information. The dashboard presents these data through interactive visualizations and analytical tools, enabling users to monitor trends and assess sectoral performance over time. Key Features of the Performance Monitoring Dashboard The Performance Monitoring Dashboard is built on a comprehensive indicator framework developed in consultation with the National Institute of Public Finance and Policy (NIPFP). The framework aligns with the Harmonized Master List (HML) of Infrastructure (2022) , issued by the Department of Economic Affairs (DEA) , which serves as the national classification framework for infrastructure sectors eligible for policy support, investment planning and financing-related benefits. Indicators have been streamlined to prevent overlap with established indices. Examples include the Index of Industrial Production (IIP) and the Eight Core Industries. A detailed indicator framework spans six infrastructure sub-sectors . These are Power, Civil Aviation, Telecommunications, Railways, Roads, and Ports, Shipping & Waterways. The Performance Monitoring Dashboard has now been expanded to 165 indicators. This expansion includes the addition of 54 new indicators, significantly enhancing the comprehensiveness of infrastructure performance monitoring. A single digital interface allows monitoring of performance sector by sector. It offers interactive visualisation and time-series analysis for policymakers, researchers and stakeholders. A centralised dashboard delivers one cross-sector view of infrastructure sectors. This capability deepens inter-sectoral analysis. The current framework gauges sectoral performance through growth rates. It reviews year-on-year, month-on-month and cumulative growth, targets and capacity utilisation in chosen sectors. Distribution of Performance Indicators Across Sub-sectors (as on 16th July, 2026) S. No Infrastructure Sub-sector Total Number of Indicators 1 Civil Aviation 31 2 Roads 8 3 Power 14 4 Ports, Shipping & Waterways 62 5 Telecommunications 13 6 Railways 37 Total 165 The Revamped Monitoring Approach The revamped approach marks a shift from measuring sectoral outputs (production) to assessing multi-dimensional infrastructure performance across the dimensions of access : which measure how widely infrastructure is available; quality : which assess its usefulness and reliability; fiscal cost & revenue : which assess allocation and use of financial resources for infrastructure; utilization : evaluate how efficiently infrastructure is used for its defined purpose; affordability : determine whether it is economically accessible to people. The above categorisation of indicators improves analysis by moving beyond simple output tracking to a more holistic evaluation of infrastructure performance across multiple dimensions, enabling informed policy decisions and targeted interventions. Engaging Stakeholders Stakeholders, including concerned Ministries and Departments, receive regular updates on their project execution. These updates draw on the data analytics generated within PAIMANA. Such analytics help them act wherever project execution needs attention. Ongoing coordination takes place through monthly review meetings and other exchanges. This practice reinforces evidence-based monitoring by providing timely updates on performance indicators. Login credentials for tailored dashboards are available with every Line Ministry and Department. Consequently, they can directly access the portal to review project progress. Infrastructure Projects Monitored (Data as of June 2026) As of June 2026, 1,847 ongoing projects were under watch across 17 Central Ministries and Departments. Together they carry a revised cost of ₹ 40.54 lakh crore . Spending on these projects has so far reached ₹ 21.97 lakh crore . This equals about 54.18 per cent of the revised cost, reflecting steady advancement. Many projects have reached advanced stages of completion. Around 709 projects (~39%) exceed 80% physical progress. About 337 projects (~19%) have passed 80% financial completion. The Transport & Logistics sector leads in the number of ongoing projects. It holds 1,341 projects worth ₹ 22.32 lakh crore , reflecting the focus on connectivity. The ongoing infrastructure projects include 769 mega projects , each costing ₹1,000 crore or more, worth ₹30.51 lakh crore . They also include 1,078 major projects , each costing ₹150–1,000 crore , worth ₹5.10 lakh crore . Ministry / Department-wise Progress of Infrastructure Projects The Ministry of Road Transport & Highways records the largest project count. It manages 1,022 projects (55%) with a revised cost share of Rs. 9.89 lakh crore (24%). The Ministry of Railways is carrying out 255 projects (14%). These carry a combined revised cost of Rs. 8.69 lakh crore (21%). The Ministry of Coal is running 121 projects (7%). Their combined revised cost stands at Rs. 2.22 lakh crore (6%). Four other ministries/departments are also implementing a significant number of projects. o The Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas is managing 105 projects with a revised cost of ₹4.33 lakh crore. o The Ministry of Power is handling 98 projects with a revised cost of ₹5.71 lakh crore. o The Ministry of Housing & Urban Affairs is implementing 50 projects with a revised cost of ₹3.65 lakh crore . o The Department of Water Resources, River Development & Ganga Rejuvenation is managing 40 projects with a revised cost of ₹2.04 lakh crore . The other 156 projects (8%) carry a combined revised cost of Rs. 4.02 lakh crore (10%). They span across several Ministries and Departments, such as Higher Education, Civil Aviation, Steel, Telecommunications, Labour & Employment, Ports, Shipping & Waterways, Health & Family Welfare, Mines, DPIIT, and Sports. Towards Data-Driven Governance The PAIMANA portal encapsulating modules of the Central repository of infrastructure projects along with outcomes as Reports/ dashboard on overview of Central sector projects costing ₹150 crores & above and the Performance monitoring dashboard would play significant stride towards transparency, efficiency and accountability. Their regular updates keep strengthening infrastructure oversight. They aid evidence-based policymaking and enable well-informed decisions. Overall, the effort promotes sustainable and inclusive infrastructure growth nationwide.
